(By Sri.H.K.Ramamurthy.,Adv)
 Judgment

Gowramma vs Ananda Kumar.D on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113201312/
1
The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries said to have sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 02.11.2021.

2. The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 02.11.2021 at about 10.00 a.m., the petitioner was walking on the left side of the road by observing all the traffic rules and regulations in front of Krishnareddy House via WhitefieldChikkathirupathi, at that time one driver of TT vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA03AB2556 which SCCH4 3 MVC No.343/2022 was driving by its driver in a rash and negligent manner endangering to human life without observing any traffic rules and regulations and dashed against the petitioner.
Due to which petitioner fell down and sustained injuries to head and all over the body.

Immediately after the accident the petitioner was shifted to RKB Hospital wherein the petitioner was admitted as an inpatient and thereafter he was shifted to St.John's Medical College Hospital wherein the petitioner admitted as an inpatient and he has spent huge amount towards hospitalization and nourishment expenses.
Prior to the accident, petitioner was very hale and healthy and was working as Coolie and she was earning a sum of Rs.20,000/ per month.

Due to the accidental injuries petitioner is not able to do his psychical work or lead a normal life as she was doing prior to the said SCCH4 4 MVC No.343/2022 accident and thereby she has suffer permanent loss of income.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle and are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, prays to award compensation of Rs.25,00,000/ with interest.
3. After service of notices the respondent No.1 is placed as exparte.

The respondent No.2 has entered appearance through its advocates and filed written statement and admitted the issuance of the insurance policy to the alleged offending vehicle, as on the date of the accident and the liability if any is subjected to terms and conditions of the policy.
The accident was taken place due to careless and negligence on the part of the petitioner.
Further denied denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner.
The compensation have claimed SCCH4 5 MVC No.343/2022 by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, the respondent No.2 has prays to dismiss the petition with cost.

4. The following issues are framed :
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, she has sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligent driving of TT Vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA03 AB2556 by its driver, in RTA took place on 02.11.2021 at about 10.00 to 10.05 a.m., on Whitefield Chikkathiru pathi Road, near Krishnareddy House, Yattakod Village, Lakkur Hobli,
Malur Taluk, Kolar?

Gowramma vs Ananda Kumar.D on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113201312/
2
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount and from whom?

3 . What Order or Award?
5.
In order to prove the claim petition, the petitioner is examined as P.W.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to 13.
Three witnesses have examined as PW.2 to 4 through them got marked documents at Ex.P.14 to SCCH4 6 MVC No.343/2022 Ex.P.25.

On behalf 2nd respondent, Sanjeev Kumar, Superintendent, RTO, Kasturi Nagar, Bengaluru East, Bengaluru is examined as RW.1,
through him got marked document at Ex.R.1.
6.
Heard the arguments of both sides and perused the material evidence that are available on record.
7. My findings on the above points are as under.

for the following:
 : R E A S O N S:

ISSUE NO.1 :
8.
That by reiterating all the averments made in the petition, the petitioner has filed his affidavit in lieu of examinationinchief, which is considered as P.W.1.

In support of his case, she has produced certified copies of FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, IMV report, wound certificate, charge sheet, notice issued to owner of the SCCH4 7 MVC No.343/2022 vehicle and reply issued by him and reply issued to the notice under section 133 of IMV Act.

All these documents are marked under Ex.P.1 to P.13.
9.

On going through the documents the petitioner's son Basavaraju.M. has lodged complaint with Malur Police on 03.11.2021 alleging that, on 02.11.2021 at about 10.00 a.m., while the petitioner was coming by walk on the left side of Whitefield Chikkathirupathi road in front of the house of Krishnareddy, the driver of the TT vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA03AB2556 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner with high speed and dashed to the petitioner.
Due to which petitioner sustained injury on her head, waist and legs.
In this regard one Rajeshreddy informed to the complainant over phone.
Immediately, the complainant came to the place of the accident, the injured was shifted RKB Sanjeeveni Hospital.
On the basis of the complaint, the police have registered FIR against the driver of the vehicle referred in the complaint.
Thereafter, the police have visited the place of the accident and drawn spot mahazar and also seized the vehicle involved in the accident.
The damages caused to alleged offending vehicle is also noted in the IMV report.
As per the wound certificate the petitioner has Gowramma vs Ananda Kumar.

D on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113201312/
3 taken treatment immediately after the accident at RKB Sanjeevini Hospital, Devalapura village,
Hosakote Taluk.
The injuries caused to the petitioner is also noted in the wound certificate.
11. The police, during the investigation have issued notice to 1st respondent to furnish the documents in respect of his vehicle involved in the accident.

After receipt of notice, the respondent No.1 issued reply stating that, he is the RC owner of the vehicle involved in the accident and at the time of the accident N.Muniraju has SCCH4 9 MVC No.343/2022 driven the said vehicle and he has possessed the driving license.

12. The police after completion of investigation have submitted the charge sheet against Muniraju,
for the offences punishable under section 279 and 337 of IPC.
The allegation made in the charge sheet as well as complaint are one and the same.

13. On behalf of the respondent No.2, Sanjeev Kumar who is working as Superintendent, RTO,
Kasturi Nagar, Bengaluru East is examined as RW.1 through him driving license extract of Muniraju.N marked at Ex.R.1.
14.
The documentary as well as oral evidence of petitioner have gone unchallenged.
As per well settled principle of law the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the abstinence of rebuttal evidence.

All the materials SCCH4 10 MVC No.343/2022 available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 02.11.2021 which is caused by the TT vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA03AB2556 which belonging to respondent No.1.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2:
15.
As already held herein above, the petitioner has proved that he has sustained injuries in RTA which is caused by respondent No.1.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.

16. To prove the nature of her injuries the petitioner has examined one Nelson.R.David, Medical Record Technician at St.Johns Hospital, Bengaluru, as PW.2, though him, authorization letter issued to him, Police intimation, MLC Register Extract, Xray Report and case SCCH4 11 MVC No.343/2022 sheet which are marked at Ex.P.14 to 18.
These documents shows that petitioner has taken treatment in St.John's Medical College Hospital, Bengaluru34.

Further, the petitioner has examined one Gowrav Chand, Medical Record Officer at Sanjeevini Hospital, Bengaluru, as PW.4, though him, authorization letter issued to him, Police intimation,
MLC Register Extract, case sheet and xray films (3 in nos) which are marked at Ex.P.21 to 25.
These documents shows that petitioner has taken treatment in RKB Sanjeevini Hospital, Hoskote Taluk, Bengaluru.

Gowramma vs Ananda Kumar.D on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113201312/
4

The petitioner has also examined Dr.S.A.Somashekara, Orthopedic Surgeon, at Bowring and Lady Curzon Hospitals, Bengaluru, is examined as PW.3, through him out patient record with reports and x ray film are marked under Ex.P.19 to Ex.P.20.

As per the evidence of PW3, the petitioner has sustained B/L SCCH4 12 MVC No.343/2022 superior and inferior pubic rami #, (Lt) sacral ala #
Denis Zone II # and Lower back moral Lavalle lesion.
Further PW.2 deposed that, petitioner has sustained total disability of Pelvis and Sacrum at 32% and that of her whole body at 16%.
According to the evidence of PW.3 the petitioner need another surgery for removal of implants which would cost around Rs.30,000/.
This aspect is not impeached during the course of cross examination.
It is also not the case of respondent that, implant is removed.
Hence, it can be considered that the petitioner is required at least Rs.20,000/ for future medical expenses.
17. According to the petitioner prior to the accident she was working as Coolie and she was earning a sum Rs.20,000/ per month.
The disability caused to the petitioner would affect on his avocation.

Considering SCCH4 13 MVC No.343/2022 this fact, I hold that the petitioner has sustained 11%
permanent physical and avocational disability.
18. The petitioner has not produced any document to prove his income.

In the absence of proof of income it is to be considered that, the notional income of the petitioner in the year 2021 was Rs.15,000/, then one day wages would Rs.500/.
19.
As per the discharge summaries produced at Ex.P.2, the petitioner was admitted as inpatient for 14 days and there was need of rest at least for a period of 46 days.
So, the petitioner is entitled compensation of Rs.60,000/ (60 days X Rs.500/ = Rs.30,000/) during the laid up period and one attendant charge at the same rate.
20. The petitioner has produced medical bills which are marked at Ex.P.4 amounting to Rs.1,83,455/.
These documents are not disproved by SCCH4 14 MVC No.343/2022 the respondents, except mere denial and there is also no reasons to disbelieve the medical bills.

Hence,
the petitioner is entitle for medical expenses.
21. As per Ex.P.1 aadhar card of petitioner the date of birth of the petitioner mentioned as 01.01.1972 and the accident has taken place in the year 2021.
So the age of the petitioner as on the date of the accident is 49 years.

22. As per Sarala Verma's case, the proper multiplier applicable to the age of petitioner is '13'.
Hence, I inclined to award future loss of income at Rs.15,000/ X 12 X 13 X 11% =Rs.2,57,400/,
which is the total loss of future income.

23. Hence, I inclined to award the compensation to the petitioner under the following heads:
1. Loss of future income Rs. 2,57,400/
Gowramma vs Ananda Kumar.D on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113201312/
5

2. Loss of income during the laid Rs. 60,000/ SCCH4 15 MVC No.343/2022 up period and one attendant charge 3. Conveyance charges Rs. 20,000/
4. Pain, sufferings and loss of Rs. 1,20,000/ amenities 5. Food and nourishment, Rs. 50,000/
6.

Medical bills Rs. 1,83,455/ Total Rs. 6,90,855/
24.
Admittedly the respondent No.1 to 2 are the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle.

Hence,
the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and the respondent No.2 insurance company shall indemnify the compensation on behalf of the respondent No.1 with interests at the rate of 6% p.a.,
Accordingly, I answer this issue partly in the affirmative.
25. ISSUE NO.4:

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
 SCCH4 16 MVC No.343/2022  ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.6,90,855/ (Rupees Six Lakhs Ninety Thousand Eight Hundred Fifty five Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.

Out of total compensation awarded to the Petitioner, 50% of the same to be released in favour of petitioner through Epayment on proper identification and remaining 50% to be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank, for a period of three years, in his name.

Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/.
Draw up award accordingly.
